metadata.title: AI Claim Denial Prevention
metadata.summary: An end-to-end healthcare claim denial prevention system combining rule checks, XGBoost risk scoring, SHAP explanations, RAG policy retrieval, and an agentic remediation planner — with FastAPI, Next.js, and a Databricks medallion pipeline.

content:
## Overview

**AI Claim Denial Prevention** predicts, explains, and remediates healthcare claim denials *before* submission to payers. It combines deterministic rule validation, XGBoost denial-risk scoring, SHAP feature explanations, RAG over insurance policy documents, and a GPT-based remediation agent.

The platform spans a Next.js dashboard, a FastAPI orchestration API, and a Databricks/GCP lakehouse with medallion feature tables and model serving. A live demo UI is available at [ai-claims-denial-prevention.vercel.app](https://ai-claims-denial-prevention.vercel.app).

Companion UI repo: [AI-Claim-Denial-Prevention-UI](https://github.com/deepesh611/AI-Claim-Denial-Prevention-UI).

## Key Features

- Rule pre-screening across referential and financial integrity checks
- XGBoost denial-risk scoring (Databricks Model Serving with local fallback)
- SHAP explanations for the top risk drivers on high-risk claims
- RAG over insurance policy docs via embeddings + vector search
- Agentic remediation plans that synthesize rules, ML, SHAP, and policy context
- Single-claim and batch CSV analysis with CSV/JSON export
- Google OAuth–gated Next.js dashboard

## Architecture

1. **Frontend** — Next.js dashboard for claim intake, batch upload, and analysis views  
2. **API** — FastAPI `/predict` pipeline coordinating rules → ML → SHAP → RAG → agent  
3. **Lakehouse** — Bronze → Silver → Gold feature tables on Databricks; MLflow model registry  
4. **Retrieval** — Policy PDFs indexed for vector search grounded remediation  

## Technologies Used

- Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, NextAuth
- FastAPI, XGBoost, SHAP, Pandas
- Databricks, Delta Lake, MLflow, Vector Search
- OpenAI embeddings + GPT-4o-mini
- Docker

metadata.title: Member Management System (Workflow-Driven Backend)
metadata.summary: A workflow-driven member management system built with React and n8n, delivered as part of a freelance engagement. Implements CRUD operations, relational data modeling, and analytics using a self-hosted stack.

content:
> **Note:** This project was developed as part of a freelance engagement. Client details have been anonymized, and only non-sensitive functionality is shown.

## Overview

This project is a **workflow-driven Member Management System** designed to replace manual and spreadsheet-based record keeping with a structured, queryable platform.

The system uses a **React + TypeScript frontend** paired with **n8n workflows acting as the backend layer**, handling CRUD operations, validation, and automation. All data is stored in a **MySQL database**, and the application is designed to be deployed in a self-hosted environment.

A public demo is provided to showcase functionality and UI behavior.

[**View Demo (Showcase Instance)**](https://dbms-with-n8n.vercel.app/)

---

## Problem This Project Solves

Organizations that rely on spreadsheets or fragmented tools often struggle with:
- Maintaining consistent member records
- Representing family and relational data
- Generating demographic insights
- Ensuring control over their data infrastructure

This project addresses those issues by providing a centralized system with structured data models, automation-driven backend logic, and built-in analytics.

---

## Core Capabilities

- **CRUD-based Member Management:** Structured creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion of member records
- **Relational Data Modeling:** Family relationships (spouse, parent, child) represented through normalized tables
- **Employment Tracking:** Storage of professional and employment-related attributes
- **Analytics & Insights:** Demographic and employment summaries rendered through dashboards
- **Image Handling:** Support for profile images via uploads or external links
- **Bulk Operations:** CSV/XLSX-based data import for migration from existing records

---

## Tech Stack

This project follows a **low-code backend / pro-code frontend** approach:

- **Frontend:** React + Vite + TypeScript
- **UI & Styling:** Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
- **Backend Logic:** n8n workflows exposed via webhooks
- **Database:** MySQL
- **Visualization:** Recharts

---

## Architecture

The system is designed around a **workflow-centric backend**:

1. **React Frontend**  
   Sends requests directly to n8n webhook endpoints.

2. **n8n Workflows**  
   Act as the API layer, handling validation, business logic, and SQL execution.

3. **MySQL Database**  
   Stores normalized relational data and supports complex queries.

This approach avoids maintaining a large custom backend codebase while keeping logic explicit and modular.

---

## Database Design

The schema is normalized to support real-world relationships:

- **Members:** Core identity and status information
- **Phones:** One-to-many contact records (primary, WhatsApp, emergency)
- **Employment:** Professional and employment details
- **Relationships:** Self-referential links defining family connections

---

## Trade-offs & Limitations

- Designed for internal or small-scale organizational use
- No authentication or role-based access control
- Workflow-based backend prioritizes flexibility over raw performance
- Demo deployment is for showcase purposes only

---

## Outcome & Learnings

- Delivered a complete CRUD-based system for a real client
- Gained experience using workflow automation as backend infrastructure
- Designed and implemented relational schemas for non-trivial data
- Balanced rapid development with maintainable system design

metadata.title: Cloud DDoS Detection using Machine Learning (Research Project)
metadata.summary: A research-focused study exploring machine learning–based anomaly detection techniques for identifying DDoS attacks in cloud environments using dataset-driven and simulated traffic analysis.

content:
## Overview

This project is a **research-focused study on detecting Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks in cloud environments** using machine learning–based anomaly detection techniques.

The work explores how abnormal traffic patterns can be identified by analyzing network behavior and how such detection mechanisms can support cloud service providers in improving availability and resilience.  
The emphasis of this project is **detection, analysis, and research**, rather than production-grade deployment or live mitigation.

---

## Problem Statement

Cloud platforms are frequent targets of DDoS attacks due to their public accessibility and shared infrastructure. These attacks aim to overwhelm cloud services with malicious traffic, leading to service degradation or outages.

Traditional rule-based security mechanisms struggle to adapt to evolving attack patterns, making **data-driven detection approaches** an important area of study for modern cloud security.

---

## Project Objectives

- Study the behavior and characteristics of DDoS attacks in cloud environments  
- Explore machine learning techniques for anomaly detection in network traffic  
- Design a conceptual detection pipeline suitable for cloud-based systems  
- Evaluate detection effectiveness using datasets and simulated traffic scenarios  

---

## Scope and Limitations

**In Scope**
- Research-oriented DDoS detection  
- Machine learning–based traffic analysis  
- Conceptual prevention and response strategies  

**Out of Scope**
- Live traffic mitigation  
- Production deployment on real cloud infrastructure  
- Real-time firewall or load balancer integration  

---

## System Architecture (Conceptual)

The proposed detection pipeline follows these stages:

1. **Traffic Data Collection**  
   Network traffic data is collected from datasets or simulated cloud traffic representing both normal and attack scenarios.

2. **Feature Extraction**  
   Relevant traffic attributes such as request rates, packet patterns, and statistical anomalies are extracted.

3. **Machine Learning–Based Detection**  
   Models are trained to differentiate between normal traffic behavior and anomalous patterns indicative of DDoS attacks.

4. **Attack Classification & Alerting**  
   Detected anomalies are classified as potential DDoS events and flagged for further analysis or response.

---

## Machine Learning Approach

The project explores **machine learning–based anomaly detection**, focusing on:

- Pattern recognition in network traffic  
- Differentiation between legitimate traffic spikes and malicious flooding  
- Adaptive learning concepts for evolving attack patterns  

Deep learning and incremental learning concepts are explored at a **theoretical and experimental level**, without large-scale neural network deployment.

---

## Tools & Technologies

- **Programming Language:** Python  
- **Domain:** Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing  
- **Techniques:** Machine Learning, Anomaly Detection  
- **Artifacts:** Research Paper, BTP Report, Documentation  

---

## Results & Observations

- ML-based detection shows promise in identifying abnormal traffic behavior  
- Data-driven approaches demonstrate better adaptability compared to static rules  
- Detection accuracy is highly dependent on dataset quality and feature selection  

> Note: Quantitative performance metrics are discussed in the accompanying research documentation rather than implemented as production benchmarks.

## Research Artifacts

- 📄 **Research Paper:**  
  https://deepesh611.github.io/DDoS-on-Cloud-Research/DDoS_Project_Paper.pdf  
  *(Content based on original project report; AI used only for language refinement and formatting.)*

---

## Future Enhancements

- Integration with real cloud traffic sources  
- Exploration of advanced deep learning architectures  
- Investigation of real-time detection and mitigation strategies  
- Honeypot-based traffic analysis as a defensive extension  

## Key Takeaway

This project demonstrates a **research-driven understanding of DDoS detection in cloud environments**, emphasizing analytical thinking, system design, and applied machine learning concepts rather than production deployment.

metadata.title: Home Server Guide
metadata.summary: A comprehensive, beginner-friendly guide to building a self-hosted home server using modern tools like Docker, Portainer, Twingate, and Nginx Proxy Manager. Walks through hardware preparation, secure remote access, containerized deployments, and service dashboards.

content:
## Overview

This project is a **comprehensive home server setup guide** that walks readers through turning a spare device — such as an old laptop, Raspberry Pi, or desktop — into a self-hosted server capable of running services like media servers, dashboards, and containerized applications.

The guide is written in a practical, beginner-friendly style and emphasizes clear, step-by-step documentation rather than abstract theory. The focus is on using modern, approachable tools to make self-hosting more accessible.

---

## Why This Guide

Setting up a home server can feel intimidating for many people due to scattered resources and complex tutorials online. This guide exists to:

- Break down the setup process into clear, incremental sections  
- Teach secure remote access without exposing open ports  
- Demonstrate how to use Docker and Portainer for service management  
- Provide examples for building a unified landing page and SSL-secured routing  

It is aimed at people who want to learn hands-on home-server setup without unnecessary jargon.

---

## What the Guide Covers

The guide leads users through the following stages:

- Preparing the hardware and flashing a Linux-based OS  
- Assigning a static IP and enabling SSH for remote management  
- Setting up secure remote access using Twingate  
- Installing Docker for managing applications as containers  
- Using Portainer's web UI to manage containers  
- Building a custom landing page for self-hosted services  
- Configuring Nginx Proxy Manager for SSL and domain routing  
- Deploying services such as media servers, file browsers, or dashboards  

Each section is designed to be accessible and practical, with links and instructions to help readers follow along at their own pace.

---

## Key Tools and Technologies

This guide demonstrates the use of:

- **Docker** for containerizing applications  
- **Portainer** for visual container management  
- **Twingate** for secure remote access without opening router ports  
- **Nginx Proxy Manager** for SSL certificates and domain routing  
- **Linux-based OS** setup for initial server configuration  
- Shell scripts and automation examples  
- Example dashboards built with Astro.js / Next.js  

These tools were selected for their usability and broad adoption in self-hosted environments, making the guide suitable for beginners and intermediate users alike.

---

## Approach and Design Decisions

- Focused on step-by-step documentation rather than software development  
- Emphasized tools that are user-friendly and reduce reliance on terminal commands where possible  
- Included secure remote access patterns to avoid common security pitfalls  
- Organized content to build confidence progressively  

The guide is a learning resource as well as a reference manual for people setting up their first home server.

---

## Limitations

- This is **not a packaged application or dashboard product**  
- It does **not include a complete automated installer**  
- The guide assumes some familiarity with concepts like networking and Linux basics  

Readers looking for hands-off "one-click" home server platforms might want to explore dedicated OS projects (e.g., CasaOS, Umbrel).

---

## Outcome & Value

- Offers a clear, structured approach to home server setup  
- Helps users gain confidence with remote access, Docker, and service management  
- Serves as a learning resource for self-hosting fundamentals  
- Provides practical steps for secure and meaningful home infrastructure

metadata.title: Multi-Agent Fraud Detection System
metadata.summary: A hybrid fraud detection platform combining rule-based analytics and AI agents to detect, investigate, and explain fraudulent insurance claims through an interactive dashboard.

content:
## Overview

The **Multi-Agent Fraud Detection System** is a hybrid AI-driven platform designed to detect, investigate, and explain fraudulent insurance claims.  
It combines **rule-based detection**, **AI-powered agents**, and an **interactive dashboard** to provide transparent and explainable fraud analysis.

The system focuses on decomposing fraud detection into specialized agents rather than relying on a single monolithic model.

---

## What the Project Includes

- **Synthetic Data Pipeline** for generating realistic insurance claims with injected fraud patterns
- **Rule-Based Detection Engine** identifying suspicious claim behavior
- **Multi-Agent Architecture**, including:
  - Detection Agent (rule-based analysis)
  - Investigation Agent (AI-driven reasoning)
  - Explanation Agent (human-readable fraud justification)
  - Query Agent (natural language search over historical cases)
- **Interactive Dashboard** for fraud analytics, claim exploration, and AI-assisted investigation
- **End-to-End Pipeline** from data generation to fraud verdict

---

## Key Features

- Hybrid fraud detection using rules and AI agents
- Explainable decisions with traceable reasoning
- Modular agent design for independent evolution
- Natural language querying of claims data
- Interactive visual analytics dashboard

---

## Architecture

The system follows a coordinated multi-agent design:

1. **Synthetic Data Generator** produces labeled claim datasets  
2. **ETL Pipeline** processes and stores data  
3. **Agent Orchestrator** coordinates agent execution  
4. **Specialized Agents** analyze, investigate, and explain fraud  
5. **Dashboard UI** presents analytics and agent outputs  

This architecture emphasizes **modularity**, **fault isolation**, and **decision transparency**.

---

## Tools & Technologies

- **Python** — core implementation
- **Streamlit** — interactive dashboard UI
- **SQLite** — data storage
- **FAISS** — vector similarity search
- **LLMs** — reasoning and explanation agents
- **Docker** — containerized execution

---

## Current Status

- Functional prototype with multiple cooperating agents
- Working dashboard for analytics and investigation
- Synthetic test data and simulated fraud scenarios
- Modular architecture ready for extension

---

## Outcome & Learnings

- Designed a real multi-agent AI system end-to-end
- Combined deterministic rules with AI reasoning
- Built explainable fraud detection pipelines
- Gained practical experience in AI orchestration and system design

metadata.title: Natural Language Data Explorer & Self-Healing Pipeline
metadata.summary: A healthcare data-exploration system on Azure Databricks with multi-agent Text-to-SQL, schema-drift handling, an AI schema advisor, role-based PHI masking, and a Streamlit interface.

content:
## Overview

An end-to-end cloud data pipeline and AI-driven exploration system built on **Azure Databricks**, designed for analysts and clinicians who need to query complex synthetic healthcare data in plain English.

The system combines three pipelines: automated ingestion into Delta Lake with drift detection, a LangGraph multi-agent Text-to-SQL path with SQL safety gates and role-based PHI masking, and an AI schema advisor that recommends and applies safe schema fixes when critical drift appears.

## Key Features

- Multi-agent Text-to-SQL over Synthea healthcare tables (analyzer, schema mapper, SQL generator, executor, evaluator, diagnostician)
- Self-healing ingestion with schema-drift severity levels and blocking remediation on critical drift
- AI Schema Advisor (GPT-4o) with DDL safety gates — autonomous `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS` only
- Role-based PHI masking at query time (doctor / analyst / sysadmin policies)
- Streamlit Data Explorer deployed as a Databricks App (chatbot, dashboard, AI advisor pages)
- Local pytest coverage for Pipeline 3 advisor logic without Spark

## Architecture

1. **Pipeline 1 — Ingestion** — Synthea CSVs from ADLS Gen2 → normalize, detect drift, write Delta tables in Unity Catalog  
2. **Pipeline 3 — AI Schema Advisor** — on critical drift, recommend/apply schema fixes and update `master_schema.json`  
3. **Pipeline 2 — Text-to-SQL** — natural-language questions → Spark SQL → PHI masking → Streamlit results  

## Technologies Used

- Python, PySpark, Azure Databricks, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog
- LangGraph / LangChain, OpenAI GPT-4o
- Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
- Streamlit (Databricks Apps)
- Pydantic, pytest

metadata.title: Tool Stash
metadata.summary: An AI-assisted software-tool catalog that researches tools, drafts structured profiles for review, and supports browsing, import/export, and recommendations — packaged with Docker Compose and multi-arch CI images.

content:
## Overview

**Tool Stash** is a personal catalog for software tools you run into day to day. An AI agent researches a tool name or URL, drafts a structured profile for review, then saves it into a searchable stash with categories, tags, and recommendations.

The stack is designed for local and self-hosted use: FastAPI backend, React/TypeScript frontend, SQLite storage, and Docker Compose with optional bundled Ollama. Images are published to Docker Hub for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

## Key Features

- Research a tool by name or URL with live web search while the agent fills a profile
- Review and edit drafted profiles before they hit the stash
- Browse, search, categorize, and tag saved tools
- AI Suggest — describe a task and get recommendations from your stash
- JSON export / import for moving a stash between machines
- Switch LLM provider and model from the UI (Ollama, Claude, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints)
- Docker Compose stacks for bundled Ollama or host-installed Ollama
- CI-published multi-arch backend and frontend images

## Architecture

1. **Frontend** — React + TypeScript UI for browse, research, review, and settings  
2. **Backend** — FastAPI service for research orchestration, persistence, and recommendations  
3. **LLM layer** — Ollama (local/bundled) or hosted providers via configurable endpoints  
4. **Storage** — SQLite database volume for the stash  

## Technologies Used

- Python, FastAPI
- React, TypeScript
- Docker, Docker Compose
- Ollama (local LLMs)
- SQLite
- GitHub Actions (multi-arch image publishing)

metadata.title: Video Summary Generator
metadata.summary: A multimodal deep learning system that generates intelligent video summaries by processing visual and audio content together at synchronized time intervals using BLIP-2 and Whisper models.

content:
## Overview

Video Summary Generator is a **multimodal deep learning application** that automatically generates intelligent summaries from video content by processing **visual and audio content together** at synchronized time intervals.  

Unlike traditional approaches that process modalities separately, this system uses **time-synchronized extraction** where each moment in the video is analyzed both visually (using BLIP-2) and aurally (using Whisper), ensuring perfect alignment between what is seen and what is heard. This synchronized approach creates richer, more accurate video summaries.

The project demonstrates advanced multimodal AI techniques, serverless GPU deployment, and production-ready ML pipeline design.

## Key Features

- **Synchronized Multimodal Processing** – Extracts (frame + audio) pairs at regular time intervals ensuring perfect audio-visual alignment
- **Advanced Visual Understanding** – BLIP-2 (2.7B parameters) generates natural language descriptions of video frames
- **Speech Recognition** – OpenAI Whisper transcribes audio segments with multiple model size options (tiny to large)
- **Intelligent Moment Selection** – Automatically identifies ~20 key moments from the video timeline
- **LLM-Based Narrative Generation** – Optional OpenRouter API integration for coherent summary narratives
- **Cloud Deployment** – Backend on Modal (serverless GPU), frontend on Streamlit Cloud
- **Production-Ready API** – FastAPI backend with proper error handling and file validation

## Technologies Used

### Deep Learning & AI
- **PyTorch** – Deep learning framework
- **BLIP-2** (Salesforce) – Multimodal image-to-text model (2.7B parameters)
- **OpenAI Whisper** – State-of-the-art speech recognition
- **Transformers** (HuggingFace) – Model loading and inference
- **OpenRouter API** – LLM-based narrative summarization

### Computer Vision & Audio
- **OpenCV** – Video frame extraction
- **FFmpeg** – Audio segment extraction and processing
- **Pillow** – Image preprocessing

### Backend & Deployment
- **FastAPI** – Modern async web framework
- **Modal** – Serverless GPU platform (T4/A10G support)
- **Streamlit** – Interactive web frontend
- **Uvicorn** – ASGI server

## Architecture

The system uses a **synchronized multimodal pipeline** with four main stages:

### 1. Synchronized Clip Extraction
- Extracts (frame + audio) pairs at regular time intervals (default: 2 seconds)
- Uses OpenCV for frame capture and FFmpeg for audio segment extraction
- Ensures perfect temporal alignment between visual and audio content

### 2. Multimodal Caption Generation
- **Visual**: BLIP-2 generates natural language descriptions of each frame
- **Audio**: Whisper transcribes speech from audio segments
- **Fusion**: Combines visual and audio captions at each timestamp

### 3. Key Moment Selection
- Intelligently selects ~20 most important moments from all multimodal captions
- Uses uniform sampling (with potential for diversity-based selection)

### 4. Narrative Summary Generation
- Creates timeline of key moments with timestamps and multimodal captions
- Optional LLM-based narrative summarization via OpenRouter API
- Fallback to formatted timeline if LLM unavailable

This **time-synchronized approach** ensures that visual and audio information are always aligned, creating more accurate and contextually rich summaries.

## Current Status

The project is **production-ready** and deployed, supporting:

- **Full multimodal pipeline** with synchronized visual and audio processing
- **Cloud deployment** on Modal (backend) and Streamlit Cloud (frontend)
- **Multiple video formats** (.mp4, .mkv, .mov) up to 500MB
- **Configurable parameters** (clip duration, target moments, Whisper model size)
- **Automatic cleanup** of temporary files and old uploads
- **GPU acceleration** with T4/A10G support on Modal

**Live Demo**: [Deployed and accessible via Streamlit Cloud](https://video-summary-generator.streamlit.app/)
**Repository**: [GitHub - Video-Summary-Generator](https://github.com/deepesh611/Video-Summary-Generator)

## Challenges and Learnings

### Technical Challenges
- **Temporal Synchronization** – Ensuring perfect alignment between visual frames and audio segments at each timestamp
- **Model Memory Management** – Loading large models (BLIP-2: 2.7B params) efficiently on GPU
- **Cold Start Optimization** – Minimizing serverless deployment latency on Modal
- **Multimodal Fusion** – Combining visual and audio captions meaningfully without redundancy
- **Error Handling** – Managing failures in audio extraction, transcription, or API calls gracefully

### Key Learnings
- Designing **time-synchronized multimodal pipelines** for better accuracy than parallel processing
- Deploying **serverless GPU applications** with Modal for cost-effective scaling
- Implementing **production-ready ML APIs** with FastAPI (validation, error handling, CORS)
- Working with **state-of-the-art models** (BLIP-2, Whisper) in real-world applications
- Building **end-to-end ML systems** from data processing to cloud deployment

This project significantly strengthened my expertise in multimodal AI, MLOps, and production ML system design.

## Outcome

Video Summary Generator is a **production-deployed multimodal AI system** that successfully combines visual and audio understanding for intelligent video summarization.

### Impact
- Demonstrates **advanced multimodal AI techniques** with synchronized processing
- Showcases **full-stack ML deployment** (FastAPI + Modal + Streamlit Cloud)
- Provides a **practical tool** for automated video content analysis
- Serves as a **portfolio piece** highlighting end-to-end ML system design

### Future Enhancements
- **Diversity-based moment selection** using embedding similarity
- **Scene change detection** for better key frame identification
- **Multi-language support** leveraging Whisper's multilingual capabilities
- **Batch processing** for multiple videos
- **Real-time streaming** support for live video analysis

This project demonstrates my ability to design, implement, and deploy **production-ready multimodal AI systems** that solve real-world problems by intelligently combining multiple data modalities.
